This question refers to a common superstition in some cultures, especially in East and Southeast Asia, regarding the New Year. The belief is that your actions and emotions during the New Year set the tone for the rest of the year. Specifically, it is said that if you cry during the New Year, you will continue to cry or be sad throughout the year. This is a superstition and not a factual statement, but according to the superstition:

Option A says you will cry for the rest of the year.
Option B says you will be sad for the rest of the year.
Option C says you will be unlucky for the rest of the year.
Option D says nothing happens.

The most commonly cited version of the superstition is that if you cry during the New Year, you will cry for the rest of the year (Option A). Option B is similar, but the superstition specifically mentions crying, not just being sad.

Answer: A
